definition: Overall Economic Freedom of the World Index score, measuring the extent to which a country’s policies and institutions support economic freedom, including personal choice, voluntary exchange, freedom to enter markets and compete, and security of privately owned property.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Size of Government area score, measuring the extent to which government spending, taxation, transfers, and state ownership affect the role of private choice and markets in the economy.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Legal System and Property Rights area score, measuring the protection of persons and legitimately acquired property, judicial independence and impartiality, enforcement of contracts, integrity of the legal system, and security of property rights.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Sound Money area score, measuring the extent to which a country provides stable money and protects individuals from substantial reductions in the value of their wealth caused by inflation and monetary instability.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Quartile classification of a country based on its overall Economic Freedom of the World Index score relative to other countries in the EFW ranking.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Categorical variable

definition: Regulation of Credit, Labor, and Business area score, measuring the extent to which regulations and government controls restrict the operation of credit markets, labor markets, and businesses.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Freedom to Trade Internationally area score, measuring the extent to which individuals and businesses are free to exchange goods, services, and capital internationally without tariffs, regulatory barriers, exchange controls, or other restrictions.
source: Fraser Institute – Economic Freedom of the World
notes: Index score, 0–10

definition: Measures entrepreneurial activity undertaken primarily because the individual has no better employment or income-generating alternative.
notes: Individual-level response; binary outcome coded as 1 = Yes and 0 = No.

definition: Measures entrepreneurial activity undertaken primarily because the individual perceives and pursues a business opportunity, rather than because there are no better employment alternatives.
notes: Individual-level response; binary outcome coded as 1 = Yes and 0 = No.

definition: Measures the proportion of adults who are actively involved in starting or running a new business. It captures individuals who are either nascent entrepreneurs or owner-managers of young businesses.
notes: Individual-level response; binary outcome coded as 1 = Yes and 0 = No.

definition: Age of the respondent at the time of the survey.
Binary indicator identifying whether the respondent personally provided funds to help someone else start a business within the previous three years.
Name of the country in which the respondent was surveyed.
Binary indicator identifying whether the respondent discontinued or shut down a business in the previous 12 months and the business did not continue its activities.
Respondent's perception of whether it is easy to start a business in their country.
notes: easystart was used for 2015–2018, where valid responses were coded as 0 = Disagree and 1 = Agree/Yes. easystartL was used for 2019 and 2021–2022, and easystartl for 2020. For the 5-point versions, responses 1–2 were recoded as 0 (No/Disagree) and responses 4–5 as 1 (Yes/Agree). Neutral responses (3 = Neither agree nor disagree), special codes, and original missing values were retained as missing.

definition: Measures the robustness of an economy through fiscal sustainability and macroeconomic stability, as well as its capacity to generate wealth through productivity, competitiveness, dynamism, labour-force engagement, and economic diversity.
Measures the enrolment, outcomes, and quality of pre-primary, primary, secondary, and tertiary education, together with the skills of the adult population.
Respondent's educational attainment classified using the GEM-harmonized education categories.
notes: Categorical: None; Some Secondary; Secondary; Post Secondary; Graduate Experience; MissingHarmonized across 2015–2022. Uses GEMEDUC for 2015–2019 and 2021–2022, and the lowercase gemeduc variable for 2020. Both variables use the same GEM education classification and value labels.

definition: Measures how easy it is for businesses to start, compete, and expand, including the regulatory and market conditions that support entrepreneurial activity.
Measures entrepreneurial intentions among individuals aged 18–64 who are not currently involved in entrepreneurship.
notes: Harmonized across GEM survey years. Based on FUTSUPNO for 2015–2019 and 2021–2022, and futsupno for 2020. The original GEM variable is specifically defined for the 18–64 population not involved in entrepreneurship.

definition: Indicates whether the respondent currently manages and owns a business that has been operating for more than 42 months.
notes: ESTBBUSO used for 2015–2019 and 2021–2022; estbbuso used for 2020.

definition: Harmonized fear-of-failure indicator covering the 2015–2022 study period.
Annual percentage growth rate of GDP at market prices based on constant local currency.
notes: Unit: Percentage (%)

definition: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP), representing the average economic output per person after accounting for differences in price levels across countries.
notes: Unit in Current international dollars

definition: Gender of the respondent.
Indicates whether the respondent believes that most people in their country consider starting a new business to be a desirable career choice.
notes: nbgoodc was used for 2015–2018. For the revised 5-point response format, nbgoodcL was used for 2019 and 2021–2022, while nbgoodcl was used for 2020. In the 5-point versions, responses of 1–2 were classified as No/Disagree, 4–5 as Yes/Agree, and 3 (Neither agree nor disagree) was retained as a separate neutral category. Original missing or non-response values were retained as missing.

definition: Measures the extent to which there are checks and restraints on government power and whether governments operate effectively and without corruption.
Measures basic healthcare services and population health outcomes, including mental and physical health, longevity, behavioural risk factors, healthcare systems, and preventive interventions.
Number of people in the respondent's household.
Indicates whether the respondent believes that people who are successful at starting a new business have a high level of status and respect in the country.
notes: nbstatus used for 2015–2018. nbstatusL used for 2019 and 2021–2022, and nbstatusl used for 2020. For the 5-point versions, responses 1–2 were coded 0 and responses 4–5 were coded 1. Neutral responses (3 = Neither agree nor disagree) and original missing/non-response values were retained as missing.

definition: Relative position of the respondent's household in the national household-income distribution, classified into three income groups.
notes: Categorical: Lowest 33%; Middle 33%; Upper 33%; Missing.GEM-recoded household income into three approximately equal national income groups. Uses GEMHHINC for 2015–2019 and 2021–2022, and gemhhinc for 2020.

definition: Measures the extent to which investments are adequately protected through property rights, investor protection, and contract enforcement, together with the availability of domestic and international capital.
Measures whether an individual personally knows at least one person who has started a business or become self-employed.
notes: Harmonized across GEM questionnaire/coding changes for 2015–2022. Based on knowent for 2015–2018, KNOWENyy for 2019 and 2021–2022, and knowenyy for 2020.

definition: Measures the basic material conditions necessary for individuals to attain a basic level of wellbeing, including material resources, nutrition, basic services, shelter, connectedness, and a safe living and working environment.
Measures the quality of infrastructure supporting trade, including communications, transport and resources, together with factors that inhibit the flow of goods and services.
Measures the extent to which individuals perceive that successful new businesses receive coverage in public media and/or the internet.
notes: Harmonized across GEM questionnaire formats. Uses nbmedia for 2015–2018; nbmediaL for 2019 and 2021–2022; nbmedial for 2020. Five-point responses are collapsed into disagreement (1–2) and agreement (4–5), while neutral responses (3) are treated as missing.

definition: Measures aspects of the physical environment that affect people's ability to flourish, including emissions, exposure to air pollution, forest, land and soil, freshwater, oceans, and environmental preservation efforts.
Respondent's current occupational status, distinguishing employment, self-employment, unemployment/non-employment, retirement, homemaking, and student status.
notes: 1 = Full-time; 2 = Part-time; 3 = Retired; 4 = Homemaker; 5 = Student; 6 = Not working; 7 = Self-employed; Missing = Non-response/missingHarmonized across 2015–2022. GEMOCCU is used for 2015–2019 and 2021–2022; gemoccu is used for 2020. The self-employed category is retained separately.

definition: Measures whether an individual perceives that there are good opportunities for starting a business in the next six months.
notes: Harmonized across GEM questionnaire/coding changes for 2015–2022. For 2015–2018, based on opport; for 2020, based on opportyy; for 2019, 2021 and 2022, the 5-point opportL measure was recoded as 1–2 = 0 (disagree), 4–5 = 1 (agree), and 3 = missing (neither).

definition: Measures the extent of basic legal rights, individual liberties, and social tolerance in a country, including freedom of assembly and association, freedom of speech and access to information, and absence of legal discrimination.
Total population of the country, representing the total number of people residing in the country.
notes: Unit: Thousands of persons

definition: Overall Prosperity Index score measuring the multidimensional prosperity of a country across social, economic, and human wellbeing dimensions.
Measures the degree to which individuals and communities are free from war and civil conflict, terrorism, politically related terror and violence, violent crime, and property crime.
Unique identifier for the respondent/observation in the GEM survey dataset.
Measures the strength of personal and family relationships, social networks, interpersonal and institutional trust, and civic and social participation within society.
Indicates whether the respondent believes that businesses primarily aimed at solving social problems are commonly seen in their country.
notes: nbsocent used for 2015–2018. nbsocentL used for 2019 and 2021–2022, and nbsocentl used for 2020. For the 5-point versions, responses 1–2 were coded 0 and responses 4–5 were coded 1.
